title: Uniswap v4's singleton design leaves two instances with a Pool ID and no contract address at all
content:
Every Uniswap v4 instance's `Contract Addresses` block contains a `Pool ID` — a 32-byte hash such as `0xe63e32b2ae40601662f760d6bf5d771057324fbd97784fe1d3717069f7b75d45` for PYUSD/USDS (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.11.1.2.2.2). For USDG/USDS (.11.3.2.2.1) and rlUSD/USDS (.11.4.2.2.1) it is the *only* child: a section titled `Contract Addresses` that contains no address.

This follows from v4's architecture. Pools are not deployed as individual contracts; they live inside one singleton, addressed by a hash of their key. There is no pool address to record and no ERC-20 LP token to hold, so the slots the template expects simply have no referent.

The Artifact absorbs this by leaving the fields empty rather than by acknowledging the difference — the `Token` identifier still names a synthetic pair label (`USDGUSDS`, `rlUSDUSDS`) that corresponds to no deployed token.

The pattern across venue types is now consistent: the Instance Configuration Document was designed around a supplied asset, a receipt token and a venue contract, and each new protocol architecture that violates one of those assumptions is accommodated by writing N/A, duplicating a slot, or leaving it blank. That keeps one schema across ten protocols, at the cost that an empty or oddly-populated field carries meaning a reader must infer from knowing how the target protocol works.
description: v4 pools have no per-pool contract, so PYUSD/USDS and USDT/USDS carry a 32-byte Pool ID alongside a Token Address, while USDG/USDS and rlUSD/USDS list only the Pool ID.
